messages.subject: Re: Deploying issue
messages.subject_clean: Deploying issue
messages.body_plain:
shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> runs on Linux hosts, so "~" is a special character in paths that refers to a user's home directory.
In shells, "$" typically prefixes environment variables.
Not sure if one or both of those are at play here, but I would recommend renaming your Excel file.

messages.body_plain:
Hey guys:

This is a weird problem I am encountering in my Shiny app. I went to a local R user mixer, and no one had a clue (well they did gave me advice to post it here):

First of all the app works totally fine in runApp() in my RStudio. But after I deploy it onto my shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> account and run it in my Chrome browser, it returns message: Error: cannot open the connection.

I did some tracking and figured out that the problem is with this line of code: form_d<-read.table(url(HTML_table[i]),fill=TRUE) with HTML_table[i] being a vector of urls linking to some SEC forms (so I guess it's not because of internet security settings).

Here are some things that I tried:
removing url(). Doesn't work.
replacing HTML_table[i] with the original url string. Doesn't work.
setInternet2(TRUE). Works when in runApp() in RStudio, but results in shiny app disconnected from server in shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.
I also made a test app, and the original line with HTML_table[i] works completely fine in the test Shiny app, both in RStudio and in shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.

Application authentication

With shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, you can limit the access to your application by enabling authentication. Only users who log-in with valid credentials will be able to view or use the app.

To enable authentication in the administrative UI, select the application to modify and click on the Users tab.

Here is a sample application with the default visibility settings:

Change the Application Visibility to Private and click on Save Settings. Changing the visibility of your application will require a restart of the application. The Owner of the account and other members of the account will automatically be included in the list of authorized users.

After the application is restarted you can add authorized users by entering their email addresses and clicking on Add User.

Each user will receive an email from shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> with an invite to view your application. If a user does not already have an authenticated account on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, they will be able to create one by authenticating through one of the following three methods:
Google Authorization
GitHub authorization
Shinyapps.io authentication

Shinyapps.io will prompt each visitor to your app for a username and password if they have not been authenticated. Only users who log-in with valid credentials will be able to view or use the app.

If you currently use the pre-beta authentication scheme, please upgrade to the new system by January 28, 2015 as we will be deprecating support for the old authentication system during the beta. For instructions on how to upgrade, please read the guide here <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/migration.html>.

Hi,

How would you test that a shiny app is deployed? I thought of using Rcurl::url.exists() which works if the app is runnin, but not if it's sleeping. For example:

> library(testthat)
>         expect_equal(
+             RCurl::url.exists('https://jhubiostatistics.shinyapps.io/recount/'),
+             TRUE
+         )

1 element mismatch
> options(width = 120)
> devtools::session_info()
Session info -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 ui       AQUA
 language (EN)
 collate  en_US.UTF-8
 tz       America/New_York
 date     2016-07-13

Packages ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 package  * version  date       source
 bitops     1.0-6    2013-08-17 CRAN (R 3.3.0)
 crayon     1.3.2    2016-06-28 CRAN (R 3.3.0)

Interactively, I can force the app to be running by using utils::browseURL() first, but that won't work when testing in a non-interactive environment. Such as with:

if(interactive()) {
    ## Open shiny app when running test in interactive mode.
    ## This will force the app to be available, which will then run the test
    ## successfully.
    browseURL('https://jhubiostatistics.shinyapps.io/recount/')
    test_that('Shiny app is up', {
        expect_equal(
            RCurl::url.exists('https://jhubiostatistics.shinyapps.io/recount/'),
            TRUE
        )
    })
}

Thank you!
Leo

messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Re: Can't deploying shiny app:Error in setwd(bundleDir) : cannot change woking directory
messages.body_plain:
Chason,
It may be easier to share a simple application that you are trying to deploy to see if we can help you spot the issue.

In looking at the error you sent it looks like something is trying to run: setwd() which seems suspicious.

Your applicaiton code shouldn't have any of the install.packages() rsconnect::setAccountInfo() etc...  It should be a ui.R and a server.R and possibly data that you are loading.  That data that you are loading from a file would need to be in a file that is in the same directory as your ui.R file and your server.R files, or in a sub directory

For example:

Your application may be in the directory: C:/Users/Chason/Desktop/Cov_test

Let us assume you have a data directory that is underneath Cov_test, so the data path looks like:  C:/Users/Chason/Desktop/Cov_test/data

If your application has a "setwd() call" it cannot contain the full path, it would need to be a relative path like so:  setwd("data")
because deploying your application to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> means it is running on a server and as such there is no C:/Users/Chason/Desktop.  The aplication will start up as if it is running with Cov_test.

Hope this helps.
-Tareef

messages.subject: Re: Error on publishing my app in shinyio
messages.subject_clean: Error on publishing my app in shinyio
messages.body_plain:
My apologies for the less than useful error message.

After digging into this, I think the issue is that you have a data file whose encoding is 'latin1', which is likely the default for your local environment which is why it works there. On shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> the default is UTF-8. You can either convert the file, or when you load it specify the encoding.

I will be filing a ticket internally so that this error is reported in a way that makes it more obvious what is going wrong.

I was having a similar problem.  Normally I build a single file shiny app but lately I have been using separate ui and server files. If you have a two file shiny app be sure to include library(DT) in both files otherwise they will fail to render.

Jon

For a number of reasons, I can't share code right now, but does anyone have any ideas why this problem would exist on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> and not locally?

ui.R
require(rCharts)
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("rCharts: Interactive Charts from R | NVD3"),

  sidebarPanel(
    selectInput(inputId = "gender",
                label = "Choose Gender",
                choices = c("Male", "Female"),
                selected = "Male"),
    selectInput(inputId = "type",
                label = "Choose Chart Type",
                choices = c("multiBarChart", "multiBarHorizontalChart"),
                selected = "multiBarChart"),
    checkboxInput(inputId = "stack",
                  label = strong("Stack Bars?"),
                  value = FALSE)
  ),
  mainPanel(
    showOutput("myChart", "nvd3")
  )
))

server.R

require(rCharts)
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  output$myChart <- renderChart({
    hair_eye = as.data.frame(HairEyeColor)
    p6 <- nPlot(Freq ~ Hair, group = 'Eye', data = subset(hair_eye, Sex == input$gender),
                type = input$type, dom = 'myChart', width = 800)
    p6$chart(color = c('brown', 'blue', '#594c26', 'green'), stacked = input$stack)
    return(p6)
  })
})

Hi Jean-Pierre,

Currently shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> does not offer persistent storage, although it is something we might offer in the future for paid accounts.

Even then, it is unlikely that we would allow incoming FTP connections.

Today, you would want to solve this problem by having your shiny application fetch the data from somewhere that you host it when the application launches.

Hello Jean-Pierre,

Another option might be a cloud-hosted database service -- mirror the daily downloads you receive at the lab, then point your Shiny app directly at the instance.

I'm getting a system online this week (AWS) which takes on-demand user data pushes rather than automatic pushes, but currently has 2 - 2,5M records, and Shiny doesn't seem too bothered.

While it's a little "old school" I like the database backend for redundancy, and have found that R plays along nicely.

Regards
Jeff

Does the application run locally for you?

What do the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> logs show? You can check them by running: rsconnect::showLogs() or by visiting the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io/> dashboard and looking at the logs under your Application tab.

Once the application is running, the metrics tab in the dashboard should indicate how much CPU and memory your application is consuming.

messages.subject: Shinyapps disconnecting from server, possibly exceeding memory limit with excel import
messages.subject_clean: Shinyapps disconnecting from server, possibly exceeding memory limit with excel import
messages.body_plain:
I created a shinyapp that displays output data from a 10,000-trial Monte Carlo simulation. The simulation is of an entire football season with 238 teams, tracking seven variables for each team in each trial (16.66+ million data points). The data from the simulation is stored in an excel file.

When I try to run the app from shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, the ui.R loads just fine, including a small portion of the excel sheet (team names in a selectInput() command). The app always crashes before any of the server.R loads (all of my read_excel() commands are at the very beginning of my server.R. This, along with some other research I've done into other example of apps crashing unexpectedly, leads me to believe my excel file is too large for shiny to handle. I have each variable stored on a separate sheet in excel, with a different read_excel() command for each sheet. I was able to get a version of the app, storing only 2 of the 7 different tracking variables, to work fine when accessing the data from separate tabs. When I tried accessing all of the data from a single tab, the app crashes like before.

The working (partial) app: https://loghan.shinyapps.io/2016_Projections/

The auto-crashing app: https://loghan.shinyapps.io/Season_Projections/

The logs for the crashing app is attached.

I have tried changing the advanced settings according to http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/scaling-and-tuning.html, to no avail.

Is there a more efficient way to import the data to shiny than excel? I don't want to use .csv files (they're the same total size anyways, so I doubt that will work), and Google sheets isn't an option because of the cell limit for a single worksheet.

App Info:
Id 111729

Thank you.

Cheers,

Kristin PJ

messages.subject: Re: How to make shinyapps.io connect to Microsoft sql server with RODBC work?
messages.subject_clean: How to make shinyapps.io connect to Microsoft sql server with RODBC work?
messages.body_plain:
I have a Microsoft SQL database within Azure and can't seem to make a connection after publishing to shinyapp.io <http://shinyapp.io>. I get the error: "first argument is not an open RODBC channel"

I've whitelisted the following IP at the firewall settings within Azure:
54.166.122.218
54.162.168.48
54.204.29.251
54.204.37.78
54.204.34.9
54.204.36.75

I've tried using the following, and all return the save error after publishing to shinyapp.io <http://shinyapp.io>
odbcDriverConnect(connection = "Driver=FreeTDS;Server=tcp:mydns.database.windows.net <http://mydns.database.windows.net>,1433;Database=mydatabase;Uid=myuserid;Pwd=mypass;Encrypt=yes;TrustServerCertificate=no;Connection Timeout=30;")
 odbcDriverConnect(connection = "Driver=FreeTDS;TDS_Version=7.0;Server=tcp:mydns.database.windows.net <http://mydns.database.windows.net>,1433;Database=mydatabase;Uid=myuserid;Pwd=mypass;Encrypt=yes;TrustServerCertificate=no;Connection Timeout=30;")
 odbcDriverConnect(connection = "Driver=FreeTDS;TDS_Version=7.2;Server=tcp:mydns.database.windows.net <http://mydns.database.windows.net>,1433;Database=mydatabase;Uid=myuserid;Pwd=mypass;Encrypt=yes;TrustServerCertificate=no;Connection Timeout=30;")
 odbcDriverConnect(connection = "Driver=FreeTDS;TDS_Version=9.0;Server=tcp:mydns.database.windows.net <http://mydns.database.windows.net>,1433;Database=mydatabase;Uid=myuserid;Pwd=mypass;Encrypt=yes;TrustServerCertificate=no;Connection Timeout=30;")

 I also tried specifying the port with Port=1433 instead of .net,1433 and tried all versions above with it but to no avail.

Does anyone have any more suggestions or ideas?

I think that more and more enterprises are starting to use Azure, and Azure is steadily adding support for R (even within SQL databases), so I hope that connecting to MS SQL database is supported within Shinyapps.io.

> The following is the error log. thanks
>
>
>

> 2015-09-26T04:12:01.158391+00:00 shinyapps[61748]:   [RODBC] ERROR: state IM002, code 0, message [unixODBC][Driver Manager]Data source name not found, and no default driver specified

Is there an example or sample code out their that allows a  set passwords for different users and use their login credentials to manipulate their view on the data within shiny ios?
Would really appreciate your help on this. Thanks!

On Tuesday, January 21, 2014 at 4:20:12 AM UTC-5, Andy Kipp wrote:
> Peter,
>
> In regards to your question about authentication, this is the feature we are currently working on. The way we expect this to work is that you will be able to configure some number of username and password combinations on a per application basis. When authentication is enabled, a visitor to your application will be prompted for his/her username and password. When the user authenticates, the information for the current session (containing the username) will be exposed to your shiny code. So, conceivably, your plan should work.
>
> Regards,
> -Andy
>
> On Wednesday, January 15, 2014 11:24:34 AM UTC, Peter Ward wrote:
> > Hi
> >
> > Just a general query about application authentication when it arrives in shinyapps. Will it go beyond the one app, one password model, i.e. will I be able to set passwords for different users and use their login credentials to manipulate their view on the data? This would obviously allow a single app to use a single copy of a data file, and I won't have to create multiple tailored apps.
> >
> > I appreciate this is similar to another recent post by Dmitri ("Some improvement ideas") but I don't think that post has any responses yet.
> >
> > Many thanks
> > Peter

messages.subject: Accessing AWS databases
messages.subject_clean: Accessing AWS databases
messages.body_plain:
Two months ago we updated our knowledge base article about accessing remote databases <https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/217592507-How-do-I-give-my-application-on-shinyapps-io-access-to-my-remote-database-> to remove the alternative for granting access to the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> AWS account number and security group and only document the whitelisting of IP addresses.

The reason for this was two-fold: first was that if the database being accessed was in an Amazon VPC and non EC-Classic, the security group alternative would not work, and second, we were planning our own transition from EC2-Classic to a VPC. By moving to a VPC and transitioning the list of IP addresses to NAT gateways, we will be able to add more servers to run more applications and not require customers to add additional IP addresses to the already public whitelist.

However, we missed a step in this process, which was to formally announce a timeframe for stopping to support granting access by security group, and for that we apologize.

As of this past Tuesday, 7/26, we completed the move of the servers hosting applications to the VPC, and as such if your application requires access to your AWS database and you previously granted permission to our account number and security group, you must switch to granting access to the list of IP addresses instead. This is also documented in our preview user guide <http://docs.rstudio.com/shinyapps.io/applications.html#accessing-your-local-databases-from-shinyapps.io>.

Again, we apologize if this has caused an inconvenience for you, but please know that we expect this to enable us to grow and scale this platform in new and interesting ways going forward.

Best,

      -- Josh

messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Does shinyapps.io support bedtools? Is there a way to install external linux tools?
messages.body_plain:
For public packages, it is possible to create an script to install additional system dependencies. See the shinyapps-package-dependencies <https://github.com/rstudio/shinyapps-package-dependencies> repo.

For private packages, there is no mechanism for installing system dependencies.

As far as calling scripts, you are welcome to include scripts in your bundle and call them from your Shiny app.

For bedtools, there is a bedr pacakge, so you could open a pull request (fasted path, alternatively you could open an issue and we will slot the work into our schedule) in the shinyapps-package-dependencies <https://github.com/rstudio/shinyapps-package-dependencies> repo for that package which installs bedtools, declare the library in your code, and then call it via the package or your scripts.

messages.subject: Re: Accessing AWS databases
messages.subject_clean: Accessing AWS databases
messages.body_plain:
Thanks you Joshua! This worked perfectly.

On Thursday, July 28, 2016 at 3:43:43 PM UTC-5, Joshua Spiewak wrote:
> Two months ago we updated our knowledge base article about accessing remote databases <https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/217592507-How-do-I-give-my-application-on-shinyapps-io-access-to-my-remote-database-> to remove the alternative for granting access to the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> AWS account number and security group and only document the whitelisting of IP addresses.
>
> The reason for this was two-fold: first was that if the database being accessed was in an Amazon VPC and non EC-Classic, the security group alternative would not work, and second, we were planning our own transition from EC2-Classic to a VPC. By moving to a VPC and transitioning the list of IP addresses to NAT gateways, we will be able to add more servers to run more applications and not require customers to add additional IP addresses to the already public whitelist.
>
> However, we missed a step in this process, which was to formally announce a timeframe for stopping to support granting access by security group, and for that we apologize.
>
> As of this past Tuesday, 7/26, we completed the move of the servers hosting applications to the VPC, and as such if your application requires access to your AWS database and you previously granted permission to our account number and security group, you must switch to granting access to the list of IP addresses instead. This is also documented in our preview user guide <http://docs.rstudio.com/shinyapps.io/applications.html#accessing-your-local-databases-from-shinyapps.io>.
>
> Again, we apologize if this has caused an inconvenience for you, but please know that we expect this to enable us to grow and scale this platform in new and interesting ways going forward.
>
> Best,
>
>       -- Josh
>
>

messages.body_plain:
I'm trying to format numbers in my shiny datatable with commas by using DT::formatCurrency. My code that generates the datatable is:
dataInput<-reactive(main())

output$table<-DT::renderDataTable(
  {withProgress(message="Compiling",
                {dataInput()[which(dataInput()$Date<=input$dates[2]&dataInput()$Date>=input$dates[1]),]}
               )
  },
  extensions=c("Buttons","FixedHeader","AutoFill","ColReorder"),
  filter="top",
  rownames=FALSE,
  options=list(searchHighlight=TRUE,
               search=list(caseInsensitive=TRUE),
               dom='Blfrtip',
               buttons=c("copy","csv","print","colvis"),
               autoWidth=TRUE,
               lengthMenu=c(25,50,100,1000),
               pageLength=25,
               fixedHeader=TRUE,
               autoFill=TRUE,
               colReorder=TRUE,
               style="width:100%"
              ),
  escape=FALSE
)

where dataInput<-reactive(main()) returns a data.frame object.

The problem is, when I add %>% formatCurrency(c(22:25,28:33),currency="",digits=0) after dataInput()[which(dataInput()$Date<=input$dates[2]&dataInput()$Date>=input$dates[1]),], it returns an error invalid argument type.

I suspect it to be dataInput() being a data.frame, but after I change it to datatable(dataInput()[which(dataInput()$Date<=input$dates[2]&dataInput()$Date>=input$dates[1]),]) and add the formatCurrency code, it returns error Error in [: incorrect number of dimensions.

Now I am completely confused. Where should I add the formatCurrency code?

I also posted this in StackOverflow: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/38642515/shiny-datatable-formatcurrency

I decided to randomly guess at setting TDS_Version, and TDS_Version=8.0 ended up working for me! (unless something happened behind the scenes on shinyapps.

The final connection request that worked was:
odbcDriverConnect(connection = "Driver=FreeTDS;TDS_Version=8.0;Server=mydns.database.windows.net <http://mydns.database.windows.net/>;Port=1433;Database=mydatabase;Uid=myuserid;Pwd=mypass;Encrypt=yes;TrustServerCertificate=no;Connection Timeout=30;")

Thanks!

messages.subject: rendering a "dot" file at shinyapps.io
messages.subject_clean: rendering a "dot" file at shinyapps.io
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I am trying to deploy the app LoopModelExplorer in the package LevinsLoops.
Runs fine at home.
The renderImage() expression creates a "dot" file,
using a function from a different package:
           LoopAnalyst:graph.cm <http://graph.cm>()
This produces a "dot" file, which I convert to gif as follows:
> system(paste("dot -Tgif -O ", dotFileCM),
>            ignore.stdout=TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE)
and return value is:
> outfile = paste0(dotFileCM, ".gif")
> list(src = outfile,
>          height=300, width=400,
>          alt = "CM should be here")
Renders beautifully when run locally.
But I can't find an executable "dot" at shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.
However, there is a directory tree
> /usr/lib/graphviz
I don't know graphviz well...
is there a way to convert from the "dot" file out there in shinyapps-system-land?
